target.title: fix: keep Gemini thinking disabled after clamp
target.body:
Closes #101785

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users requesting a Google/Gemini reasoning level that the selected model clamps down to `off` could still get thinking enabled at the provider's high effort level.

AI-assisted: yes, created with Codex.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Google shared provider now treats `clampThinkingLevel()` returning `off` as a disabled-thinking result before mapping provider efforts. The existing `max` to `high` normalization remains in place for supported non-off Google thinking requests.

## User Impact

Gemini requests whose catalog/model constraints resolve reasoning to `off` no longer unexpectedly send high thinking settings, avoiding unwanted token overhead and provider errors on models that should have thinking disabled.

## Evidence

- `git diff --check` passed.
- `/Users/fallmonkey/Developer/openclaw/node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check --threads=1 packages/ai/src/providers/google-shared.ts packages/ai/src/providers/google-shared.test.ts` passed from the linked worktree using the main checkout's installed formatter.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs packages/ai/src/providers/google-shared.test.ts` passed as a narrow local fallback after temporarily symlinking this linked worktree to the main checkout's existing `node_modules`: 1 test file, 7 tests, 1 Vitest shard in 3.49s. The symlink was removed after the run.
- Redacted provider payload trace from the actual Google shared request builder passed on head `8b9ac468207528fe66e4f213b5cb0ca5c63b2cce`. The trace used `buildGoogleSimpleThinking()` plus `buildGoogleGenerateContentParams()` with off-only `thinkingLevelMap` metadata and no API key or network call. It verifies the clamped-off path emits disabled simple thinking and does not send `HIGH` or `includeThoughts` in the Google payload:

```json
{
  "model": "gemini-2.5-flash",
  "requestedReasoning": "max",
  "simpleThinking": { "enabled": false },
  "providerPayloadThinkingConfig": { "thinkingBudget": 0 },
  "proofChecks": {
    "disabledAtSimpleThinkingLayer": true,
    "noHighThinkingLevel": true,
    "noThoughtsRequested": true,
    "gemini25UsesZeroBudgetWhenDisabled": true
  }
}
{
  "model": "gemini-3-flash-preview",
  "requestedReasoning": "xhigh",
  "simpleThinking": { "enabled": false },
  "providerPayloadThinkingConfig": { "thinkingLevel": "MINIMAL" },
  "proofChecks": {
    "disabledAtSimpleThinkingLayer": true,
    "noHighThinkingLevel": true,
    "noThoughtsRequested": true
  }
}
{
  "model": "gemini-3-flash-preview",
  "requestedReasoning": "max",
  "simpleThinking": { "enabled": false },
  "providerPayloadThinkingConfig": { "thinkingLevel": "MINIMAL" },
  "proofChecks": {
    "disabledAtSimpleThinkingLayer": true,
    "noHighThinkingLevel": true,
    "noThoughtsRequested": true
  }
}
```

- PR checks for head `8b9ac468207528fe66e4f213b5cb0ca5c63b2cce` passed for `Real behavior proof`, `Workflow Sanity`, `CI / runner-admission`, `Labeler`, `iOS Periphery Dead Code`, Socket security, and the security/dependency guard checks that apply to this draft/fork PR. The broad CI matrix jobs were skipped by the workflow policy for this context.
- Remote agent proof was attempted before PR creation but is blocked in this environment: Blacksmith Testbox is unavailable because the `blacksmith` executable is missing, and brokered AWS Crabbox requires login/configuration.
- One local autoreview pass was run with `/Users/fallmonkey/Developer/openclaw/.agents/skills/autoreview/scripts/autoreview --mode local`; it reported clean with no accepted/actionable findings.
